import parse

# Test __contains__ with various scenarios

# 1. Named field only
r = parse.parse('{name}', 'hello')
print('=== Named field only ===')
print('Result: ' + str(r))
print('\"name\" in r: ' + str('name' in r))   # key check
print('\"hello\" in r: ' + str('hello' in r))  # value check
print('\"z\" in r: ' + str('z' in r))           # not found

# 2. Fixed field only
r2 = parse.parse('{}', 'hello')
print()
print('=== Fixed field only ===')
print('Result: ' + str(r2))
print('0 in r2: ' + str(0 in r2))              # index check
print('\"hello\" in r2: ' + str('hello' in r2))  # value check
print('\"z\" in r2: ' + str('z' in r2))          # not found

# 3. Mixed fields
r3 = parse.parse('{n} {}', 'x y')
print()
print('=== Mixed fields ===')
print('Result: ' + str(r3))
print('\"n\" in r3: ' + str('n' in r3))         # key check
print('0 in r3: ' + str(0 in r3))               # index check
print('\"x\" in r3: ' + str('x' in r3))         # named value
print('\"y\" in r3: ' + str('y' in r3))         # fixed value
print('\"z\" in r3: ' + str('z' in r3))         # not found

# 4. Match object
p = parse.Parser('{w}')
m_obj = p._match_re.match('hello')
if m_obj:
    mw = parse.Match(p, m_obj)
    print()
    print('=== Match object ===')
    print('Match: ' + str(mw))
    print('\"w\" in mw: ' + str('w' in mw))       # key check
    print('\"hello\" in mw: ' + str('hello' in mw))  # value check
    
# 5. search returns Result directly
r4 = parse.search('{n}', 'the number is 42')
print()
print('=== search result ===')
print('Result: ' + str(r4))
print('\"n\" in r4: ' + str('n' in r4))
print('\"42\" in r4: ' + str('42' in r4))
" 2>&1 | tail -30
